title: Ringtones, an Overdrawn Card and Cellulant's Turn to Banking
conflicts: Founding year: 2004 in Njoroge's own words and Business Daily, against 2002 or 2003 in other profiles; the story uses 2004. Why ringtones stalled: operators' 80 per cent cut (Business Daily 2016), airtime billing difficulty (Business Daily 2023, company executive), phones storing their own music (The Standard 2021, a later period); the story gives the first two, attributed. Outcome numbers: How we made it in Africa (2010) gives 16,000 ringtones sold on day one at KSh 75 but about KSh 60,000 a month in the first year, and both six million and 12 million customers; none of these is used. Bank counts (50 in 2016, 60+ in 2023, about 100 in 2021) are used only with the 2016 date.
notes: Quote stance: complicates. Sources do not date each step of the change; the story dates only the M-Pesa launch (March 2007) and reported profitability (2007), so approx_date is 2007, not the slate's 2006. No single documented day exists for the change, so the story opens with the 2004 founding and the first board meeting. Wikipedia used once, only for the M-Pesa launch date. TechCabal, cellulant.io and carolmusyoka.com block automated requests.
